It’s early October now, just after the National Day holiday. The summer maize is all cut and dried — we got about 950 jin per mu this year, which is decent, though the price at the grain dealer is still only around 1.1 yuan per jin, same as last year. Doesn’t matter; we need the cash for buying inputs. Our household is three people: my husband, me, and our son. But our son works in a factory in Handan and only comes back for a few days during wheat harvest and maize sowing. So for most of the year it’s just us two old folks managing the 10 mu of land, and we’re not young anymore — my back gives me trouble when I bend too long.

I’ve been farming this same plot for 30 years, wheat and maize, back to back. I only went to primary school, so I don’t read those extension pamphlets. I do what I’ve always done, and I watch what my neighbors do. Old Wang down the road has about the same land as us, and his wheat usually looks better than mine because he spends more on fertilizer, but he also has his son living at home to help. We can’t do everything he does.

**Wheat:** The maize stalks are cleared and I hired Old Zhang’s tractor for rotary tilling — 50 yuan per mu, but you can’t plant without tilling. I buy the improved wheat seed from the supply shop in town. I don’t save my own seed; the yield drops and it’s not worth the risk. It costs about 35 yuan per mu. I plant around October 12th to 15th, when the soil is still warm enough. For fertilizer, I put down half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base — that’s about 25 kg. Then in spring, when the wheat turns green and looks a bit yellow, I topdress with urea, about 15 to 20 kg per mu. Last year I only used 15 kg because fertilizer prices were high, and the yield was lower. This year I’ll do closer to 20 kg — I’d rather waste a little money than lose a whole crop. Total nitrogen is roughly what the shopkeeper says is 14 kg per mu. I don’t know the exact phosphorus and potassium, but it comes out of the compound bag.

Irrigation is the big cost. Pumping from our tube well costs about 35 to 40 yuan each time per mu. For wheat I try to irrigate three times: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing in March, and once when the heads come out in April. Last year I skipped the winter irrigation to save money, and I regretted it because spring was dry. This year I’ll do all three if I can, but if the electricity bill looks too high in spring, I might cut one. I spray herbicide in spring — the weeds are terrible — and keep an eye out for aphids. For labor, my husband and I put in about 8 days on the wheat, but for harvest we hire 4 days of help because we can’t keep up with the threshing and drying. I expect about 900 jin per mu if the spring rain is good, though last year we only got 850 jin.

**Maize:** The wheat comes off in early June with a combine — we hire it, about 60 yuan per mu — and we have to get the maize in the ground almost immediately. Sometimes we only have three or four days! I buy hybrid seed every year, about 50 yuan per mu. Because the window is so tight, I put down compound fertilizer and urea all at once when planting. If I have time and the rain comes right, I might topdress once more at the big trumpet stage, but honestly last year I didn’t manage it and the maize was still okay. So usually one application, sometimes two. I use a bit less fertilizer on maize than wheat — nitrogen around 12 kg per mu, with some phosphorus and potassium from the compound bag.

For maize irrigation, usually twice: once in June if it doesn’t rain, and once in August when the kernels are filling. But if the summer rains are good, maybe only once. I spray herbicide at planting and watch for corn borer — if I see damage, I spray insecticide, but I try not to spend too much on chemicals. For labor, it’s about 6 family days, and we hire 3 days for harvest because my back can’t handle carrying those heavy maize ears like it used to. I expect about 950 jin per mu.

**Money:** Everything adds up. Seed, fertilizer, irrigation pumping, pesticide, hired labor, machine costs for tilling and harvesting — it comes to about 6,200 yuan for the year. That’s a lot for us. We have to keep some cash for my husband’s medicine and for emergencies. I’d love to put more fertilizer on like Old Wang does, but we just can’t afford it. We do enough to be safe, not enough to be the best.
